attributes.action: Add chronic mental health illness with excessive distress to Assisted Dying bill
attributes.additional_details:
This would be for people who are unable to function for significant periods of time due to their mental health, who have explored over many years a large number of treatments,& who have stuck to any medication schedules. 
Excluding one off acute mental health issues or anyone under 25.
There would need to be a threshold of numbers of acute mental health episodes while on treatment for the option of assisted death to be available, maybe a proportion of life and not a fixed arbitrary number.
attributes.background: Having suffered from chronic mental health issues since a very young age, which have been treatment resistant and cause significant distress to me for over 40 years, I would like people who are in the same situations as myself to be included as people who could request access to be allowed to die.

rejection.details:
You submitted this petition before the House of Commons declined to give a Second Reading to the Terminally Ill Adults Bill on 11 September. 

You may wish to submit another petition setting out measures that you might wish the Government to take.
